title: Philadelphia Fed December 2026 Livingston Survey, 10:00 a.m. ET — the calendar's only scoreable professional-forecaster S&P 500 target, on a release date whose scheduling rule just broke three editions running
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) by this event's own never-assessed initial research — the Philadelphia Fed's own release calendar, whose embedded structured data carries the row verbatim as {"title":"December Livingston Survey","month":"december 2026","day":"11","displayMonth":"Dec","year":"2026","time":"10:00 a.m."}, and exactly two Livingston rows for 2026 matching the survey's published June/December cadence (the other: Jun 24, 10:00 a.m.). The calendar feed's accuracy for THIS release is corroborated from two Livingston-SPECIFIC primaries that the proposal filing this id could not reach: the survey's own landing page (philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/livingston-survey, HTTP 200, 48,255 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-09) reads 'Last updated: June 24, 2026, 10:00 a.m. ET', and the bank's Livingston-specific release-date file (livingston-release-dates.xlsx, HTTP 200, 22,357 bytes) lists the June 2026 survey at exactly 2026-06-24 — so the calendar's June row is exact against the publisher's own dedicated record. NEITHER Livingston-specific source publishes a forward December date: the xlsx lists surveys already released (last row 2026-06) and the landing page carries only the most recent release, which is why this stays EST: rather than being upgraded. Filed estimate on three counts: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), this lane never self-confirms, and no Livingston-specific page names 2026-12-11. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, after reading the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/livingston-survey-2026-12-11.from-philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25.json, filed 2026-09-09 by the PIES lane), now shadowed. That proposal assigned this file two tasks and put a DECLINE explicitly on the table. Both are answered, and the answer to the second is KEEP-BUT-RELOCATE. Task (a), re-verify date and time from a Livingston-specific page rather than the shared calendar row: PARTIAL, and honestly so — the survey's own landing page and the bank's livingston-release-dates.xlsx both pin the JUNE 2026 edition to 2026-06-24 10:00 a.m. exactly as the calendar says, which validates the feed, but neither publishes a forward December date, so 2026-12-11 remains a calendar-row read and stays `estimate`. Task (b), does a survey whose only claim is a shared date earn an entry: the COLLISION does not, and the entry does. The collision is the fragile part. 2026-12-11 is precisely what 'the Friday two days after the December FOMC decision' predicts (FOMC 2026-12-09, confirmed), a rule that reproduced the release date for 15 of 16 consecutive editions from June 2017 through December 2024 — and has then MISSED all three most recent editions (Jun 2025 actual Tue 06-24 vs rule Fri 06-20; Dec 2025 actual Fri 12-19 vs rule Fri 12-12; Jun 2026 actual Wed 06-24 vs rule Fri 06-19). So the date that puts this print on the cliff is a return to a rule currently 0-for-3, and if the 2025-2026 regime holds instead, a December 2026 release lands nearer 12-18 and the collision premise evaporates entirely. What earns the row is something the proposal did not know the survey contains: SPIF, a live median S&P 500 LEVEL forecast at 6-month, 12-month and year-end horizons — the only scoreable professional-forecaster index target anywhere on this calendar. This session scored 84 of them from the publisher's own medians.xlsx over the accurate-base era (June 2004 onward), with realized year-end closes taken from the file's own BY column: MAE 13.90% against a random walk's 18.27% but a DEAD HEAT with random-walk-plus-drift (14.13%); implied forecast growth +9.26% mean, sd 5.54, against realized +15.16%, sd 20.71; 81 of 84 forecasts pointed up while the index fell 14 times; and at the 12M, 1Y and 2Y horizons the panel is 62-for-62 forecasting a HIGHER index, having never once called a down year. The measured content of this instrument is a drift constant of roughly +6-7%/yr with 13-17% error bars, and that is a standing base rate worth carrying against any forecaster index target this app ever renders. Impact LOW and symbols [] deliberately: semiannual, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is macro-keyed, no tracked name carries a forecaster-survey channel, and the publisher's own base-period rule fixes the December content to information available at 2026-10-31 (daily variables) and October 2026 (monthly), with the questionnaire mailed in November — so the print reports a view formed BEFORE the 12-09 FOMC, BEFORE the 12-10 CPI and BEFORE the cliff resolves. The day's market relevance belongs to cr-expiry-2026-12-11 and the index events, never to this. This is an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
